title.value: Recurrent Traumatic Brain Injury Surveillance Using Administrative Health Data: A Bayesian Latent Class Analysis
title.justification: The title is extracted directly from the header of the document.
title.quote: Lasry O, Dendukuri N, Marcoux J and Buckeridge DL (2021) Recurrent Traumatic Brain Injury Surveillance Using Administrative Health Data: A Bayesian Latent Class Analysis. Front. Neurol. 12:664631. doi: 10.3389/fneur.2021.664631

analysis.description: The paper evaluates the accuracy of administrative health data (AHD) surveillance case definitions for recurrent traumatic brain injury (rTBI) using Bayesian latent class analysis. It estimates the 1-year rTBI incidence adjusted for measurement errors across different age groups without relying on a gold standard rTBI definition.

type.justification: The paper is based on studying actual data obtained from administrative health records and employs Bayesian latent class models to analyze this data, indicating empirical research.
type.quote: We used Bayesian Latent Class Models (BLCMs) to simultaneously assess the accuracy of the four surveillance case definitions defined above (conceptual diagram shown in eFigure 1).
